real_estate.homebuilder: Rates eased to 7.19% while single-family construction jumped 7.6% in August and pending home sales edged up 0.3%.
real_estate.commentary:
Rates eased back. Mortgage News Daily's Thursday readings put the 30-year at 7.19% and the 15-year at 6.81%, down from Wednesday's one year highs of 7.24% and 6.84%. The 10-Year closed Thursday at 4.94%, down 0.07, though it was back at 5.00% this morning.

Builders picked a lane in August. The Census Bureau reported total housing starts at 1,275,000 a year, down 2.6% from July, but single-family starts rose 7.6% to 918,000 while apartment building fell 22.5% to 344,000. Worth knowing before anyone leans on those numbers: Census puts a margin of plus or minus 12.0% on the total and plus or minus 14.0% on the single-family gain, so neither monthly move is big enough to be certain it happened.

Buyers came back a little. The National Association of REALTORS® said pending home sales rose 0.3% in August to an index of 71.2, still 4.7% below a year ago. The West led the month at plus 3.0%, and Lawrence Yun noted buyers "steadily entered into contracts in August even though mortgage rates increased."

• The local math: at Fremont's median list price of $1,209,392, a 20% down loan is $967,514, under Alameda County's $1,249,125 high-balance conforming limit.
• At 7.19%, principal and interest run about $6,561 a month, $33 less than at Wednesday's 7.24%, and every eighth of a point is about $82.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Board wide: 2,771 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 191 coming soon and 205 brand new.
• Five city ledger: 723 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 637 are already on the market and 86 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 262 live, 207 active, 38 coming soon, 17 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,209,392 at $797 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 29 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 186, Milpitas 119, Newark 90, Union City 66.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,099,999 at $685 a square foot. 283 homes are priced under a million, and 158 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

What this means for you: the ledger jumped to 723 from 708, the biggest one day gain in weeks, and Union City added five more. Homes sitting 60 days or longer held at 158. Buyers: more choice arrived this week and rates backed off, so it is a reasonable week to write. Sellers: you now have 15 more competitors than Thursday, so condition and price do the talking.

stocks.news:
Thursday was a strong session, led by the Nasdaq. Friday opened softer, with the S&P and the Dow lower and the Nasdaq flat.

Nvidia did the heavy lifting, closing up 2.54% at $219.34 after Jensen Huang said the company will sell twice as many AI chips next year as this year. At 24.1 billion shares outstanding, that close puts Nvidia near $5.3 trillion in market value.

About today's chart: Nvidia's reported revenue went from $60.9 billion in fiscal 2024 to $215.9 billion in fiscal 2026, and the company guided in August to about 70% growth for fiscal 2028. That guidance is a growth rate, not a dollar figure. Applied to the roughly $396 billion analysts expect for this fiscal year, it works out to about $673 billion; applied to higher estimates, closer to $700 billion. The version of this chart going around prints $673 billion as if Nvidia had said it.

feature_images.alt: Bar chart of Nvidia's total annual revenue by fiscal year: $60.9 billion in fiscal 2024, $130.5 billion in fiscal 2025 and $215.9 billion in fiscal 2026 as reported, an analyst consensus of about $396 billion for fiscal 2027, and a range of $673 billion to $700 billion for fiscal 2028 from the company's guidance of about 70% growth.
feature_images.caption: Nvidia's reported revenue through fiscal 2026, then the analyst consensus for this year and what the company's 70% growth guidance implies for next year.
feature_images.source: Source: Nvidia revenue from SEC filings; fiscal 2027 analyst consensus and the fiscal 2028 implications as reported by Fortune, August 26, 2026.

economy.note: All four are Thursday, September 17. The 10-Year is the Treasury daily yield curve close, gold and silver are the COMEX front month at Thursday's 1:00 PM PT print measured against Wednesday's same time print, and Brent is the ICE front month settlement. Friday so far: at 7:45 AM PT gold was $4,390.90, silver $66.78 and Brent was trading near $100.02, a live tick and not a settlement, with the 10-Year back at 5.00%.
economy.commentary:
China's share of the containers coming through the Port of Los Angeles has fallen from 61% in 2020 to about 40% this year, and most of that drop happened in the last year alone. The port's own figures show the same story in dollars: China and Hong Kong cargo was worth $120 billion in 2024 and $82 billion in 2025, a 32% drop. For us, that is the supply chain behind local goods prices and industrial space quietly rerouting through Mexico, Canada and Southeast Asia.

One caution on that 40%. It comes from a June 30 analysis of Port of Los Angeles and FreightWaves data, which labels the year an estimate. The graphic going around calls it a September confirmation from the port, and we could find nothing that confirms it, so we show it as an estimate.

Layoffs stayed low. New unemployment claims fell 10,000 to 196,000 for the week ending September 12, with 1.73 million people still collecting benefits.

Metals ran. At Thursday's 1:00 PM PT print gold rose 1.81% to $4,380.60 and silver 3.62% to $65.72, and both were higher again Friday morning. Brent settled at $104.82, down 0.95%, and was trading near $100 this morning.

A note on the newsletter's numbers: it had the 10-Year at 4.93%, down 0.01, where Treasury shows a 4.94% close, down 0.07. It had Brent at $104.15, down 0.66%, where the settlement was $104.82, down 0.95%. And it had gold down 0.20%, where the same time prints show a 1.81% gain. Silver was left out again.

feature_images.alt: Line chart of China's share of containerized imports through the Port of Los Angeles: 61% in 2020, 58% in 2021, 56% in 2022, 54% in 2023, 53.4% in 2024 and 2025, and an estimated 40% in 2026.
feature_images.caption: China's share of the Port of Los Angeles import boxes has fallen 21 points since 2020, with the steepest drop in the past year. The 2026 figure is an estimate.
feature_images.source: Source: Port of Los Angeles and FreightWaves data compiled by VIZION, June 30, 2026; trading partner values from the Port of Los Angeles.

crypto.commentary:
Live quotes pulled at 7:55 AM PT with 24 hour changes. All three are sharply higher, with XRP up about 7%.

Crypto rallied after the SEC granted a five year "innovation exemption" on Thursday, letting qualifying venues trade tokenized U.S. stocks on public blockchains without registering as exchanges. Tokenized shares have to carry the same voting and dividend rights as the real thing, and companies can block third parties from tokenizing their shares.

A note on the newsletter: its Bitcoin figure checks out, but against Wednesday at the same hour Ether was up 1.72%, not 0.69%, and XRP was down 0.47%, not up 0.81%.
